title: KV pageframe anchoring and continuous batch coordinator prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a prototype that reduces GPU OOMs and tail latency for long-context workloads by (1) anchoring contiguous blocked KV segments into transient pageframes while a micro-batch completes, and (2) coordinating continuous batching windows to increase token-affinity and prefetch accuracy. This ticket covers the design, prototype implementation, measurements, and a small rollback-safe rollout plan.

Context: Current paged/blocked KV approach frequently evicts small fragmentary blocks under bursty continuous batching, causing extra host-GPU migration work and token-latency spikes. We observed that short-lived contiguous runs are common for multi-turn chat workloads; grouping and anchoring them for the lifetime of the current micro-batch improves locality and reduces re-fetches.

High-level approach:
- Pageframe anchoring: allocate an anchor descriptor for contiguous block ranges (aligned to 4-8MB tunable frame). When a micro-batch touches blocks that coalesce into >= anchor_threshold, create an anchor and pin it on GPU for anchor_duration tied to coordinator signals. Anchors are admitted as a single unit to eviction and migration pipelines.
- Continuous batch coordinator: a lightweight in-node coordinator that tracks in-flight micro-batches, token-affinity maps for tenant/route, and emits hints to the allocator (anchor/demote/prefetch) at sub-ms granularity. The coordinator adapts anchor_duration based on recent miss-rate and latency SLO.
- Graceful demote policy: when host memory pressure or preemption occurs, demote anchors in cardinality order (largest anchors first) and coalesce writeback if multiple anchors originate from same host page to reduce PCIe transfers.
- Prefetch hints: coordinator sends host prefetch hints for upcoming anchors based on token-affinity predictions and small LRU-based lookback. Prefetch conservatively overlaps with batch processing to avoid increasing tail latency.

Non-goals: full multi-tenant fairness scheduler and cross-node anchor migration. Those will be follow-ups after prototype results.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype reduces repeated GPU re-fetch of the same contiguous KV ranges by >= 40% on representative multi-turn chat load; 2) 95th percentile token latency improves or stays within 5% of baseline SLO for target batch sizes; 3) end-to-end GPU memory OOMs caused by KV churn are eliminated in the local stress harness for 30-minute load tests; 4) telemetry emitted for anchor create/destroy, demote, and prefetch events with counts and bytes; 5) implementation gated behind feature-flag and safe rollback path documented.
implementation_notes:
- Allocator changes: add anchor metadata (start_block, block_count, frame_id, pin_epoch). Anchor lifetime is bound by pin_epoch and coordinator heartbeat. Anchor admission must be atomic wrt eviction scanner to avoid double-eviction.
- Coordinator: in-process thread with an async ring to the serving path; accepts lightweight tokens for batch start/end and returns anchor_duration hints. Provide a no-op coordinator variant for canarying.
- Eviction & migration: extend existing migration pipeline to accept anchor units; coalesce NVMe/host writebacks by grouping anchors mapping to same host pages.
- Telemetry: counters and histograms for anchor_create, anchor_eviction, anchor_demote_bytes, anchor_prefetch_hits, anchor_prefetch_misses, coordinator_lag_ms. Export via existing runtime metrics endpoint.
- Config knobs: anchor_threshold_blocks (default 64), anchor_frame_size_bytes (default 4MB), min_anchor_duration_ms (default 10), max_anchor_duration_ms (default 200), coordinator_window_ms (default 8).
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for anchor allocation, atomic admission, and demote coalescing; 2) Integration harness: replay multi-turn chat traces with spikey arrival patterns to validate reduced re-fetch and stability; 3) Microbench: synthetic token streams to measure 50/95/99 latency with and without anchoring; 4) Fault injection: simulate coordinator lag and ensure feature-flag shuts off anchors cleanly; 5) Long-run soak test: 2x nominal throughput for 30 minutes verifying no OOMs and bounded migration bandwidth.
rollout_plan:
Phase A: internal prototype build behind feature flag on staging nodes (2 GPUs) and run integration traces. Phase B: enable selective canary for low-traffic tenant routes with coordinator no-op fallback. Phase C: widen to half of staging with anchors on for bursty routes only. Phase D: monitor for 48h and then gate to runtime-1.22 release for broader rollout. Quick rollback: flip feature flag to disable anchors and let eviction revert to block-level behavior.
Metrics to watch: anchor_prefetch_miss_rate < 20%, anchor_demote_bytes per minute, p99 token latency, migration PCIe throughput, OOM count per host.
